title: Matrices: shape, traversal, and linear storage
goal: Map two coordinates to an index and validate rectangular shape before computing.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.one-dimensional-arrays. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: Two coordinates
paragraphs: A matrix has rows rows and cols columns. Element (r,c) is valid when 0<=r<rows and 0<=c<cols. In std::array<std::array<int,3>,2>, the outer size is two rows and the inner size is three columns. A built-in int a[2][3] is also an array of rows.

a[r][c] first selects a row and then its element. Swapping indices does not safely transpose an arbitrary matrix: rectangular dimensions may produce out-of-bounds access. Check both coordinates independently.

sections.title: Nested traversal
paragraphs: The outer loop visits rows; the inner loop visits columns in the current row. Set rowSum=0 before the inner loop and initialize total once before both loops. Mixing these state levels leaves only the final row’s sum.

With rows*cols elements, a complete traversal is O(rows*cols). If either dimension is zero, there are no elements. The lab explicitly permits zero dimensions so the algorithm never depends on a[0] existing.

sections.title: A coordinate into an index
paragraphs: The final position (1,2) in 2x3 gives index 5.
steps: Read the contract and independently derive the expected result for the given input.
Trace state after each significant operation and identify the established preconditions.
Run the source, compare stdout and exit code, then check the additional cases.

sections.title: A flat buffer
paragraphs: In row-major storage, the index is r*cols+c. The preceding r rows occupy r*cols positions, then c selects a column. In a 2x3 matrix, (1,2) maps to 5, the last of six elements. This follows from the representation rather than a magic conversion.

vector<int> data(rows*cols) creates elements, unlike reserve. Validate dimensions before multiplying. Dimensions up to 10 give at most 100 elements; values in -1000…1000 have an absolute total at most 100000.

sections.title: Rectangularity and nested vectors
paragraphs: vector<vector<int>> can contain rows of different lengths. Its type does not establish rectangularity. Before running a matrix algorithm, verify that every row has cols elements; define cols separately when the outer vector is empty.

Flat storage simplifies the total size but requires an indexing formula. Nested storage exposes rows clearly but gives each row a separate owned buffer. Choose a representation for the required operations rather than bracket appearance.

sections.title: Transposing 2x3
paragraphs: The new 3x2 shape needs a new width in its indexing formula.
steps: Read the contract and independently derive the expected result for the given input.
Trace state after each significant operation and identify the established preconditions.
Run the source, compare stdout and exit code, then check the additional cases.

sections.title: Rows, columns, and transposition
paragraphs: A column sum fixes c and varies r. A square matrix’s main diagonal has r==c; a rectangular generalization has length min(rows,cols) if the contract defines it that way. Never assume square shape without validation.
A transpose has cols rows and rows columns. Write result[c*rows+r]=data[r*cols+c] into a new buffer. An in-place transpose requires another algorithm and is not an implicit requirement here.

sections.title: Shape tests
paragraphs: A square example can hide reversed dimensions. Include 2x3 and 3x2, one row, one column, and a zero dimension. Label original positions with distinct values to expose permutations.

Keep a table of (r,c,index,value), expected sums, and operation counts. Incomplete or excess input must reject the whole record as invalid. Next, character sequences introduce another distinction: a byte, a character, and a terminator are different things.

practice.title: Laboratory: Matrices: shape, traversal, and linear storage
practice.task: Read rows and cols in 0…10 and exactly rows*cols integers in -1000…1000. Print the total and a line of row sums; with rows=0 the second line is empty.
criteria: The contract matches the task and defines units, empty input, and extra data.
Every published case matches and two explained original tests are included.
Establish the shape before applying an index formula.
Do not test matrix code only with a square shape. Do not obtain cols from a[0] when there are no rows.
Source, actual output, exit code, and a justified complexity explanation are preserved.
practice.hint: Establish the shape before applying an index formula.

steps.action: Restate the input, output, and rejection contract in your own words.
Draw the state and state the invariant: Establish the shape before applying an index formula.
Start from the scaffold, implement the valid path, then add boundary checks.
For every reference case, independently write the expectation before running; keep stdout and exit code.
Add two original cases including one rejection; explain the result without consulting the reference.
Preserve source, a result table, and a short cost-and-limit analysis.
